text: The number of complex numbers $z$, satisfying $|z|=1$ and $\left |\frac{z}{\bar{z}}+\frac{\bar{z}}{z}\right |=1$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $|z|=1$, write $z=e^{iθ}$ with $θ\in [0,2π)$, so $\bar{z}=e^{-iθ}$ and

$\frac{z}{\bar{z}}+\frac{\bar{z}}{z}=e^{2iθ}+e^{-2iθ}=2\cos 2θ$

The condition $|2\cos 2θ|=1$ gives $\cos 2θ=\pm \dfrac{1}{2}$, with $2θ\in [0,4π)$.

For $\cos 2θ=\dfrac{1}{2}$: $2θ=\dfrac{π}{3},\dfrac{5π}{3},\dfrac{7π}{3},\dfrac{11π}{3}$, so $θ=\dfrac{π}{6},\dfrac{5π}{6},\dfrac{7π}{6},\dfrac{11π}{6}$.

For $\cos 2θ=-\dfrac{1}{2}$: $2θ=\dfrac{2π}{3},\dfrac{4π}{3},\dfrac{8π}{3},\dfrac{10π}{3}$, so $θ=\dfrac{π}{3},\dfrac{2π}{3},\dfrac{4π}{3},\dfrac{5π}{3}$.

These give 8 distinct numbers: $z=\pm \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\pm \dfrac{1}{2}i$ and $z=\pm \dfrac{1}{2}\pm \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
Let $\mathrm{X}=𝐑\times 𝐑$. Define a relation R on X as :

$(a_{1},b_{1})R(a_{2},b_{2})⇔b_{1}=b_{2}$

Statement I: $\mathrm{R}$ is an equivalence relation.

Statement II : For some $(\mathrm{a},\mathrm{b})\in \mathrm{X}$, the $\mathrm{set}\mathrm{S}=\{(x,y)\in \mathrm{X}:(x,y)\mathrm{R}(\mathrm{a},\mathrm{b})\}$ represents a line parallel to $y=x$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For any $(a,b)\in X$, $b=b$, so $(a,b)R(a,b)$ and R is reflexive.

If $(a_{1},b_{1})R(a_{2},b_{2})$, then $b_{1}=b_{2}$, so $b_{2}=b_{1}$ and $(a_{2},b_{2})R(a_{1},b_{1})$; R is symmetric.

If $(a_{1},b_{1})R(a_{2},b_{2})$ and $(a_{2},b_{2})R(a_{3},b_{3})$, then $b_{1}=b_{2}=b_{3}$, so $(a_{1},b_{1})R(a_{3},b_{3})$; R is transitive. Hence R is an equivalence relation and Statement I is true.

For a fixed $(a,b)\in X$, $(x,y)R(a,b)$ holds exactly when $y=b$, so

$S=\{(x,b):x\in \mathrm{ℝ}\},$

which is the horizontal line $y=b$ with slope $0$. The line $y=x$ has slope $1$, so S is never parallel to $y=x$ and Statement II is false.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: If the area of the region $\left \{(x,y):-1\leq x\leq 1,0\leq y\leq \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{e}^{|x|}-\mathrm{e}^{-x},\mathrm{a}>0\right \}$ is $\frac{\mathrm{e}^{2}+8\mathrm{e}+1}{\mathrm{e}}$, then the value of $a$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $-1\leq x\leq 0$, $|x|=-x$, so the upper boundary is $y=a+e^{-x}-e^{-x}=a$; this part is a rectangle of area $a\times 1=a$.

For $0\leq x\leq 1$, $|x|=x$, so the upper boundary is $y=a+e^{x}-e^{-x}$, which stays positive since $a>0$ and $e^{x}\geq e^{-x}$.


[IMG]

$\text{Area}=a+\int\limits _{0}^{1}(a+e^{x}-e^{-x})dx=a+[ax+e^{x}+e^{-x}]_{0}^{1}=2a+e+\dfrac{1}{e}-2$

The given area is $\dfrac{e^{2}+8e+1}{e}=e+8+\dfrac{1}{e}$, so

$2a-2=8\Rightarrow a=5$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: Let the range of the function $f(x)=6+16\cos x\cdot \cos \left (\frac{π}{3}-x\right )\cdot \cos \left (\frac{π}{3}+x\right )\cdot \sin 3x\cdot \cos 6x,x\in 𝐑$ be $[α,β]$. Then the distance of the point $(α,β)$ from the line $3x+4y+12=0$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Using $\cos (A-B)\cos (A+B)=\cos ^{2}A-\sin ^{2}B$:

$\cos \left (\frac{π}{3}-x\right )\cos \left (\frac{π}{3}+x\right )=\frac{1}{4}-\sin ^{2}x=\cos ^{2}x-\frac{3}{4}$

$\cos x\cos \left (\frac{π}{3}-x\right )\cos \left (\frac{π}{3}+x\right )=\frac{4\cos ^{3}x-3\cos x}{4}=\frac{1}{4}\cos 3x$

Therefore

$f(x)=6+4\cos 3x\sin 3x\cos 6x=6+2\sin 6x\cos 6x=6+\sin 12x$

Since $-1\leq \sin 12x\leq 1$, the range of $f$ is $[5,7]$, so $(α,β)=(5,7)$.

The distance of $(5,7)$ from $3x+4y+12=0$ is

$\frac{|3(5)+4(7)+12|}{\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}}=\frac{55}{5}=11$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: The distance of the line $\frac{x-2}{2}=\frac{y-6}{3}=\frac{z-3}{4}$ from the point $(1,4,0)$ along the line $\frac{x}{1}=\frac{y-2}{2}=\frac{z+3}{3}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The line through $(1,4,0)$ parallel to $\dfrac{x}{1}=\dfrac{y-2}{2}=\dfrac{z+3}{3}$ has direction $(1,2,3)$; its general point is $(λ+1,2λ+4,3λ)$.

A general point of $\dfrac{x-2}{2}=\dfrac{y-6}{3}=\dfrac{z-3}{4}$ is $(2t+2,3t+6,4t+3)$.

At the point of intersection, $λ+1=2t+2$ and $2λ+4=3t+6$, so $λ=2t+1$ and $2(2t+1)+4=3t+6\Rightarrow t=0,λ=1$.

The $z$-coordinates also agree ($3λ=3=4t+3$), so the lines meet at $(2,6,3)$.

The required distance is

$\sqrt{(2-1)^{2}+(6-4)^{2}+(3-0)^{2}}=\sqrt{1+4+9}=\sqrt{14}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: If in the expansion of $(1+x)^{\mathrm{p}}(1-x)^{\mathrm{q}}$, the coefficients of $x$ and $x^{2}$ are 1 and -2 , respectively, then $\mathrm{p}^{2}+\mathrm{q}^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(1+x)^{p}(1-x)^{q}=\left (1+px+\dfrac{p(p-1)}{2}x^{2}+\ldots \right )\left (1-qx+\dfrac{q(q-1)}{2}x^{2}-\ldots \right )$

Coefficient of $x$: $p-q=1$.

Coefficient of $x^{2}$: $\dfrac{p(p-1)}{2}-pq+\dfrac{q(q-1)}{2}=-2$

$\Rightarrow p^{2}+q^{2}-2pq-(p+q)=-4\Rightarrow (p-q)^{2}-(p+q)=-4$

$\Rightarrow 1-(p+q)=-4\Rightarrow p+q=5$

So $p=3$, $q=2$, and $p^{2}+q^{2}=9+4=13$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: A rod of length eight units moves such that its ends $A$ and $B$ always lie on the lines $x-y+2=0$ and $y+2=0$, respectively. If the locus of the point $P$, that divides the rod $AB$ internally in the ratio $2:1$ is $9\left (x^{2}+αy^{2}+βxy+γx+28y\right )-76=0$, then $α-β-γ$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Let $A(t,t+2)$ lie on $x-y+2=0$ and $B(s,-2)$ on $y+2=0$. The point $P(h,k)$ dividing $AB$ internally in the ratio $2:1$ is

$h=\dfrac{2s+t}{3},k=\dfrac{2(-2)+(t+2)}{3}=\dfrac{t-2}{3}.$

Hence $t=3k+2$ and $s=\dfrac{3h-t}{2}=\dfrac{3h-3k-2}{2}$.

Then $t-s=\dfrac{9k-3h+6}{2}=\dfrac{3(3k-h+2)}{2}$ and $(t+2)-(-2)=t+4=3(k+2)$.

$AB=8$ gives

$\dfrac{9(3k-h+2)^{2}}{4}+9(k+2)^{2}=64\Rightarrow 9\left [(3k-h+2)^{2}+4(k+2)^{2}\right ]=256.$

Expanding, $(3k-h+2)^{2}+4(k+2)^{2}=h^{2}+13k^{2}-6hk-4h+28k+20$, so

$9\left (h^{2}+13k^{2}-6hk-4h+28k\right )+180=256\Rightarrow 9\left (x^{2}+13y^{2}-6xy-4x+28y\right )-76=0.$

Comparing, $α=13$, $β=-6$, $γ=-4$, so $α-β-γ=13+6+4=23$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: Let $\int x^{3}\sin x\mathrm{d}x=g(x)+C$, where $C$ is the constant of integration. If $8\left (g\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )+g^{'}\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )\right )=απ^{3}+βπ^{2}+γ,α,β,γ\in Z$, then $α+β-γ$ equals :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \int x^{3}\sin xdx=-x^{3}\cos x+\int 3x^{2}\cos xdx \\ =-x^{3}\cos x+3x^{2}\sin x-\int 6x\sin xdx \\ =-x^{3}\cos x+3x^{2}\sin x+6x\cos x-6\sin x+c \end{array}$

So $g(x)=-x^{3}\cos x+3x^{2}\sin x+6x\cos x-6\sin x$

$\begin{array}{l} g\left (\dfrac{π}{2}\right )=\dfrac{3π^{2}}{4}-6 \\ g^{'}(x)=x^{3}\sin x \\ g^{'}\left (\dfrac{π}{2}\right )=\dfrac{π^{3}}{8} \\ 8\left (g\left (\dfrac{π}{2}\right )+g^{'}\left (\dfrac{π}{2}\right )\right )=π^{3}+6π^{2}-48 \end{array}$

So $α+β-γ=55$

$(1,0)&(5,0)$ will be the end points of diameter

$\Rightarrow Eq^{\mathrm{n}}$ of circle is

$\begin{array}{l} (x-1)(x-5)+y^{2}=0 \\ x^{2}+y^{2}-6x+5=0 \end{array}$

text: Let $x=x(y)$ be the solution of the differential equation $y=\left (x-y\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}y}\right )\sin \left (\frac{x}{y}\right ),y>0$ and $x(1)=\frac{π}{2}$. Then $\cos (x(2))$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Multiplying the equation by $dy$:

$y~dy=(xdy-ydx)\sin \left (\dfrac{x}{y}\right )$

Dividing by $y^{2}$ and using $d\left (\dfrac{x}{y}\right )=\dfrac{y~dx-xdy}{y^{2}}$:

$\dfrac{dy}{y}=-\sin \left (\dfrac{x}{y}\right )d\left (\dfrac{x}{y}\right )$

Integrating: $\ln y=\cos \left (\dfrac{x}{y}\right )+C$.

At $y=1$, $x=\dfrac{π}{2}$: $0=\cos \dfrac{π}{2}+C$, so $C=0$ and $\ln y=\cos \left (\dfrac{x}{y}\right )$.

At $y=2$: $\cos \left (\dfrac{x(2)}{2}\right )=\ln 2$, so

$\cos (x(2))=2\cos ^{2}\left (\dfrac{x(2)}{2}\right )-1=2(\ln 2)^{2}-1$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: Let $α,β$ be the roots of the equation $x^{2}-\mathrm{ax}-\mathrm{b}=0$ with $\mathrm{Im}(α)<\mathrm{Im}(β)$. Let $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{n}}=α^{\mathrm{n}}-β^{\mathrm{n}}$. If $\mathrm{P}_{3}=-5\sqrt{7}i,\mathrm{P}_{4}=-3\sqrt{7}i,\mathrm{P}_{5}=11\sqrt{7}i$ and $\mathrm{P}_{6}=45\sqrt{7}i$, then $\left |α^{4}+β^{4}\right |$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$α+β=a$ and $αβ=-b$. Since $α^{2}=aα+b$, multiplying by $α^{n-2}$ gives $α^{n}=aα^{n-1}+bα^{n-2}$; the same holds for $β$, and subtracting:

$P_{n}=aP_{n-1}+bP_{n-2}$

For $n=5$: $11\sqrt{7}i=a(-3\sqrt{7}i)+b(-5\sqrt{7}i)\Rightarrow -3a-5b=11$

For $n=6$: $45\sqrt{7}i=a(11\sqrt{7}i)+b(-3\sqrt{7}i)\Rightarrow 11a-3b=45$

Solving, $b=-4$ and $a=3$, so $α+β=3$ and $αβ=4$.

$α^{2}+β^{2}=(α+β)^{2}-2αβ=9-8=1$

$α^{4}+β^{4}=\left (α^{2}+β^{2}\right )^{2}-2(αβ)^{2}=1-32=-31$

So $\left |α^{4}+β^{4}\right |=31$.

Hence, the answer is 31.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: The focus of the parabola $y^{2}=4x+16$ is the centre of the circle $C$ of radius 5 . If the values of $λ$, for which C passes through the point of intersection of the lines $3x-y=0$ and $x+λy=4$, are $λ_{1}$ and $λ_{2},λ_{1}<λ_{2}$, then $12λ_{1}+29λ_{2}$ is equal to $________$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$y^{2}=4(x+4)$

Equation of circle

$(x+3)^{2}+y^{2}=25$

Passes through the point of intersection of two lines $3x-y=0$ and $x+λy=4$ which is $\left (\frac{4}{3λ+1},\frac{12}{3λ+1}\right )$, after solving with circle, we get

$\begin{array}{l} λ=-\dfrac{7}{6},1 \\ 12λ_{1}+29λ_{2} \\ -14+29=15 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: The number of ways, 5 boys and 4 girls can sit in a row so that either all the boys sit together or no two boys sit together, is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
All boys together: the 5 boys form one block, which with the 4 girls makes 5 units, arranged in $5!$ ways; the boys inside the block are arranged in $5!$ ways. Number of ways $=5!\times 5!=14400$.

No two boys together: the 4 girls are arranged in $4!$ ways, leaving 5 gaps (including both ends). The 5 boys must occupy all 5 gaps, one in each, in $5!$ ways. Number of ways $=4!\times 5!=2880$.

The two cases cannot happen together, so the required number $=14400+2880=17280$.

Hence, the answer is 17280.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: The roots of the quadratic equation $3x^{2}-px+q=0$ are $10^{\text{th}}$ and $11^{\text{th}}$ terms of an arithmetic progression with common difference $\frac{3}{2}$. If the sum of the first 11 terms of this arithmetic progression is 88 , then $q-2p$ is equal to $________$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \begin{array}{l} S_{11}=\dfrac{11}{2}(2a+10d)=88 \\ a+5d=8 \\ a=8-5\times \dfrac{3}{2}=\dfrac{1}{2} \end{array} \\ \text{Roots are} \\ \begin{array}{l} \mathrm{T}_{10}=\mathrm{a}+9\mathrm{d}=\dfrac{1}{2}+9\times \dfrac{3}{2}=14 \\ \mathrm{T}_{11}=\mathrm{a}+10\mathrm{d}=\dfrac{1}{2}+10\times \dfrac{3}{2}=\dfrac{31}{2} \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{p}}{3}=\mathrm{T}_{10}+\mathrm{T}_{11}=14+\dfrac{31}{2}=\dfrac{59}{2} \\ \mathrm{p}=\dfrac{177}{2} \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{q}}{3}=\mathrm{T}_{10}\times \mathrm{T}_{11}=7\times 31=217 \\ \mathrm{q}=651 \\ \mathrm{q}-2\mathrm{p} \\ =651-177 \\ =474 \end{array} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: The variance of the numbers $8,21,34,47,\ldots ,320$ is $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \begin{array}{l} \mathrm{Var}(8,21,34,47,\ldots \ldots ,320) \\ \mathrm{Var}(0,13,26,39,\ldots \ldots ,312) \\ 13^{2}\cdot \mathrm{Var}(0,1,2,\ldots \ldots ,24) \\ 13^{2}\cdot \mathrm{Var}(1,2,3,\ldots \ldots ,25) \end{array} \\ \text{So,}σ^{2}=13^{2}\times \left (\dfrac{25^{2}-1}{12}\right )=8788 \\ \text{Alternate solution} \\ \begin{array}{l} 8+(n-1)13=320 \\ 13n=325 \\ n=25 \end{array} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{no. of terms}=25 \\ \begin{array}{l} \text{mean}=\dfrac{\sum \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}}{\mathrm{n}}=\dfrac{8+21+\ldots +320}{25}=\dfrac{\frac{25}{2}(8+320)}{25} \\ \text{variance}σ^{2}=\dfrac{\sum \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}^{2}}{\mathrm{n}}-(\text{mean})^{2} \\ =\dfrac{8^{2}+21^{2}+\ldots .+320^{2}}{25}-(164)^{2} \\ =8788 \end{array} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift
